closed.content: Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

Cleanup done. Summary of what I found and changed in the atlas memory (space `eval`, 117 live claims):

**Merged genuine duplicates** (same fact stated twice/thrice in different words):
- Two claims about the test runner → merged into: *"The atlas test suite is run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used."*
- Three claims about deployment → merged into: *"atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root; the old make deploy target no longer exists."*

**Removed stale, session-scoped facts** that had outlived their relevance (idle 40 days, tagged fast-decay, no longer meaningful):
- "The branch under review is spike/consolidate."
- "The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api."

**Left alone (false positives):** The consolidation tool flagged ~20 more pairs as "contradictions" and one 8-member "near-duplicate" cluster, but on inspection almost all of them were just topically-related facts sharing the `atlas` entity tag (e.g. billing cadence vs. billing support routing, container registry vs. distroless base image) — not actual conflicts or restatements. I didn't touch those.

One pair is worth flagging rather than silently resolving: *"Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more"* vs. *"Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so cargo check --all-features has to pass."* These read as genuinely different claims about "feature flags" — one about runtime rollout flags, one about Cargo's compile-time `--features`. I left both stored since they likely describe two distinct mechanisms, but if you know atlas only has one kind of feature flag, let me know which description is right and I'll correct the other.
